contentList.content: Marks weapons and armor as Bad, Not Ideal or Good for one character. Off removes every mark.

Items in inventory, container and trade slots are rated for one character, a
companion's items and a trader's stock included. While trading, that is the party member chosen in the trade window. Otherwise it is your selected character. Equipped items are rated for their wearer. For a Pact of the Blade or Hexblade warlock, a melee weapon they aren't
proficient with is Not Ideal rather than Bad, since binding it makes them
proficient.

Shows a badge on equipped weapons and armor that are Bad or Not Ideal for their
wearer. The badge uses that rating's Badge icon and Color from the Looks tab. Good items get none.
Explain equipped item badges on hover

Hovering the badge on an equipped item shows why it is Bad or Not Ideal, such as
Not proficient: Longswords.

Hovering the badge or dot on an item in an inventory, container or trade window
shows why it is Bad or Not Ideal, such as Not proficient: Longswords. Good items have no tooltip.
Gives Wares the same marks as other items. Off leaves Wares unmarked.

How marks show on items in a Trade window, on your side and the trader's. Equipped items keep their badges.
Full: the same marks as everywhere else.
Subtle: no Dim or Gray, and the Glow, Badge and Dot at 65% strength.
Off: no marks.

Off: prints any warnings and errors to the Script Extender console, and a line
with your settings when a save loads.
Basic: also writes a log file, and prints a short line when items are rated or a
setting changes.
Verbose: also writes a sample of individual item ratings to the log file.

Log files go to
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Larian Studios\Baldur's Gate 3\Script Extender\ProficiencyAtAGlance. Each save you load starts a new file, and old files are kept.
Items the character isn't proficient with are always Bad. Choose the rating each penalty below gives; when several apply, the worst wins. Hover a setting to see what it marks.
The rating these penalties give an item. Off ignores them.

Marks shields, non-clothing body armor, and Medium or Heavy helmets, gloves, and
boots for a monk, since Unarmored Movement doesn't work in them.

Marks heavy body armor for a barbarian, since Rage and Fast Movement don't work
in it.
The rating these penalties give an item. Off ignores them.
Monk: Heavy or Two-Handed melee weapon

Marks Heavy and Two-Handed melee weapons for a monk, since attacks with them
grant no Bonus Unarmed Strike.

Marks non-Finesse melee weapons for a rogue, since Sneak Attack needs a Finesse
or ranged weapon.
The rating these penalties give an item. Off ignores them.

Marks non-Finesse main-hand melee weapons for a Defensive Duelist, since the
feat's reaction needs a Finesse weapon.

Marks main-hand melee weapons other than Reach weapons, quarterstaffs, and
spears for a Polearm Master, since the feat's bonus and opportunity attacks need
one of those.

Marks Two-Handed weapons while an off-hand item is equipped, and the reverse,
since equipping either unequips the other. Off ignores them.

Drawbacks read from items' Boosts and the game's rules, so a mod that lifts a limit also removes the matching mark. Choose the rating each gives; when several apply, the worst wins. Hover a setting to see what it marks.
The rating these penalties give an item. Off ignores them.

Marks non-clothing body armor and Medium or Heavy helmets, gloves, and boots,
plus shields for a monk, since wearing any of them ends the feature's AC bonus.

Marks non-clothing body armor and Medium or Heavy helmets, gloves, and boots
while Mage Armor is active, since wearing armor ends it.

Marks shields, non-clothing body armor, and Medium or Heavy helmets, gloves, and
boots that would end another equipped item's AC bonus, as with Bracers of
Defense. The item already in the same slot doesn't count.

Marks body armor whose Dexterity cap is below this character's Dexterity
modifier, so the armor's AC leaves part of the bonus unused. A higher cap from Medium Armor Master counts.

Marks items that lower this character's Armor Class, when the drawback depends
on the wearer, such as on their abilities, race or feats, or on what else they
wear.

Marks items that would end an AC bonus or an AC formula from one of this
character's passives or equipped items, when its condition reads what the
character wears, such as a mod's version of Unarmored Defense. A worn item that keeps the bonus off is marked too. The bonuses above keep their own checkboxes.

When a mark comes only from these AC penalties, the badge shows the game's AC
shield icon instead of the rating's Badge icon.

Marks items that would lower this character's movement speed or jump distance,
read from Boosts and their conditions, such as armor that slows anyone below its
Strength requirement. A drawback every wearer pays is under Drawbacks for every wearer. Monk Unarmored Movement is under Armor vs class features, on the Class & feats
tab. Off ignores them.

Marks items that lower this character's movement speed or jump distance, when
the drawback depends on the wearer, such as on their abilities, race or feats,
or on what else they wear.

Marks items that would end a movement speed bonus from one of this character's
passives or equipped items, when its condition reads what the character wears. A worn item that keeps the bonus off is marked too.

Marks items that would lower one of this character's ability scores, read from
Boosts and their conditions. A drawback every wearer pays is under Drawbacks for every wearer. Off ignores them.

Marks items that lower one of this character's ability scores, when the drawback
depends on the wearer, such as on their abilities, race or feats, or on what
else they wear.

Marks items that would end an ability score bonus from one of this character's
passives or equipped items, when its condition reads what the character wears. A worn item that keeps the bonus off is marked too.

Marks items that would worsen this character's attack rolls, saving throws,
ability checks, initiative, damage, critical hits, hit points, spell save DC or
resources, or give attacks against them Advantage, read from Boosts and their
conditions. A drawback every wearer pays is under Drawbacks for every wearer. Off ignores them.

Marks items that worsen this character's combat stats (attack rolls, saves,
checks, damage, hit points, spell save DC and the like), when the drawback
depends on the wearer, such as on their abilities, race or feats, or on what
else they wear.

Marks items that would end a combat bonus (to attack rolls, saves, damage, hit
points and the like) from one of this character's passives or equipped items,
when its condition reads what the character wears. A worn item that keeps the bonus off is marked too.

Marks items with a drawback that anyone wearing them pays, whatever their
abilities or race. Off by default, since such a drawback is part of the item rather than a poor fit
for this character.
Marks armor that gives Disadvantage on Stealth checks. Medium Armor Master removes the mark wherever it removes the Disadvantage.

Marks items whose Boosts or passives worsen the AC, movement, ability scores,
rolls, damage, hit points or resources of anyone wearing them, such as a mod's
attack roll penalty on heavy armor.

Choose how each rating marks an item, so Bad, Not Ideal, and Good items stand out at a glance.

Glow, Badge, and Dot use the rating's Color: Glow is a band fading in from the slot's edge, Badge is a small icon on a dark background in one corner, and Dot is a small dot in the opposite corner. Dim darkens the item, and Gray drains most of its color, rarity border included. On equipped items, Bad and Not Ideal show only the badge, and Good shows nothing.
Which corners the badge and the dot sit in, on equipped items too.
